new.analysis:
Last week was a full miss on running. All three planned walk-run sessions were skipped, and the rest days were kept, so nothing was overrun. Your weekly report gives no reason for the gap, and your body check and sleep look fine.

The week before, you ran all three sessions, so the habit is still there. The planned week stepped up from 63 minutes of walk-running to 75 minutes, which may have been too big a jump after the early September cold.

A week away costs some fitness, but the base is still there, so this is a short restart. The plan returns to lengths you have already run and adds no hard session yet.

Your 5K goal depends on how fast the run blocks grow from 2 minutes. Running the whole distance by Nov 15 needs about 40 minutes of continuous running, which is a big climb in about six weeks.

That is only achievable with three runs most weeks, so consistency matters more than any single session. The checkpoint is the week of Oct 12: if you are running 5-minute blocks by then, the whole-distance goal is on track. If the blocks are still near 2 to 3 minutes, I will recommend a run-walk finish and say so plainly.

Build usually adds threshold work, but a week back after a gap is the wrong time for hard efforts. Harder work starts the week of Oct 5, when the run blocks move up from 2 to 3 minutes.

Keep the rest days real, and walk the run blocks whenever effort goes past 7 out of 10. If a cough or fever returns, stop running and see a doctor before you restart.
